newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohap to take over BASF tape unit.
newsitem.headline: Kohap to take over BASF tape unit.

text.p: Germany's BASF AG said on Tuesday South Korea's Kohap group would be taking over its worldwide magnetic tape products business from January 1 next year.
BASF said in a statement that the consideration for the acquisition was not being revealed.
BASF said more information about the sale would be made available at a news conference on Wednesday at 1100 GMT.
On October 16, BASF said three foreign firms had been interested in acquiring the ailing tape unit.

Although BASF had signed a letter of understanding with the Turkish group RAKS Holding, promising them exclusive rights to the tape unit in late summer, the company's supervisory board had demanded that other potential buyers be considered.
BASF's supervisory board had expressed concern that RAKS was too small and questioned its ability to run Magnetics, one of the world's best known tape brands.
Magnetics posted sales of 1.5 billion marks last year and employs 3,700 workers, but had been posting losses for some time.
BASF said the Magnetics workers would be informed of the decision on Tuesday and Wednesday.
